components.description: Player/Library/Queue/Setup; Material NavigationBar or CupertinoTabBar, current selection and restorable destination index. iPhone fixed-height labels do not scale; reading content scales.

components.name: Library and queue row
components.description: Material ListTile or CupertinoButton row with folder/music icon, wrapping title/subtitle and folder chevron. Row identity includes destination, source scope, rendered revision and item ID. Library playback checks rendered revision/scope and current playable ID/title membership; queue playback checks rendered revision and current ID/title membership. Parent/page/assisted navigation remain distinct.
components.pageScrollRestoration: At f5f5a03, Library PageStorageKey includes source scope, revision, current/returned parent, page and loading state; Queue includes source scope, revision and offset. Status/error/busy do not change list identity. Same-location offsets can restore without another folder/page/revision inheriting them.
components.assistedPageRecovery: At 31047c22, matching Mango assisted selection completion, timeout/send failure or connection loss retires only that page while retaining cached rows and offset. Stale row/Back/more actions disable; explicit fresh-root browsing recovers. No playback replay or native Mango/Apple selection-route change.

components.name: Scrollable connection and recovery
components.description: Player retains live-region status, adaptive errors and pending explanation in its ListView; guided Setup uses its own phase heading, guidance and errors in scrolling content. Library/Queue put status messages in the separate stable browsing status viewport; disconnected Open Setup recovery remains in destination content, with capability-specific guidance.

components.name: Stable browsing status viewport
components.description: Library/Queue reserve independently scrollable live-region status/error/pending space above their independent destination ListView, with a one-logical-pixel divider. Status changes do not reflow music rows; long messages scroll without overlaying rows. Uses incumbent Material/Cupertino text and error roles, without a browser approximation.

layout.statusScrollIdentity: Current status, error, busy state and library invalidation; a changed message or invalidation resets the status scroll viewport.
layout.assistedRecoveryCopy: Page expired after selection. Tap Browse source library.

components.name: Optional Mango companion test
components.description: Existing Kotlin system controls for optional folder settings and local DX340 tests. Scrolling path/limitations, case-preserved assisted labels, disabled unsupported rows with an explicit nativeTestable diagnostic exception, and empty-folder Back guidance. AlertDialog confirms file selection; separate audible-result actions distinguish listening from request success. No new tokens or browser approximation.

components.name: Retained Kotlin action
components.description: Companion/native reference Button. Reference-only; not the shared Flutter action.

components.name: Retained Kotlin destinations
components.description: Native reference four-button row; selected-state/raw-pixel layout debt remains. Not the shared phone NavigationBar.

components.name: Retained SwiftUI playback
components.description: Native reference borderless SF Symbol action with spoken label. Retained for parity reference; not the shared Cupertino phone action.

narrative.overview:
The user selected native system appearance, then one shared Android/iPhone interface on 28 October 2026. Flutter/Dart now owns the phone screens, using stock Material controls on Android and Cupertino controls on iPhone. Light/dark appearance, system typography and familiar control states provide the visual identity. No custom screen palette, typeface or approved comp was introduced.

The shared phone implementation uses Flutter 3.41.4/Dart 3.11.1 above Kotlin Android Bluetooth/foreground-service and Swift CoreBluetooth/restoration code. The DX340 companion and source adapters remain Kotlin; the later Watch client remains native SwiftUI. Existing Kotlin and SwiftUI phone apps are retained as parity references. Their tokens below are explicitly scoped to those references and the companion, rather than applied to Flutter.

Both finish reviewers returned ship for their supplied disconnected captures only: Android dark/default-font screens and the six iPhone simulator states described below. This records the implemented system and those narrow verdicts. Whole-product, physical phone, connection stability and accessibility acceptance remain open.

The optional Mango folders setting and local test surface extend the companion's existing system appearance. A separate reviewer returned ship only for nine DX340 dark/default-font states. That host review does not change the shared phone direction or broaden either earlier phone verdict.
keyCharacteristics: One maintained phone presentation with platform-adaptive system controls.
Large labeled playback actions with authorization and capability-dependent states.
Player, Library, Queue and Setup as stable bottom destinations.
Scrolling connection, recovery and source explanations that follow actual state.

rules.name: The System Color Rule
rules.body: Let platform-adaptive theme roles supply screen colors and control states; keep the launcher palette scoped to the launcher.

dos: **Do** use stock Material/Cupertino appearance and system theme roles for the shared phone.
**Do** preserve scalable reading content, semantic labels and the authored minimum action target.
**Do** keep Player, Library, Queue and Setup stable and connection guidance scrollable.
**Do** let authorization, source capability and pending state decide available actions.
**Do** retain companion/native-reference tokens in their stated scope until parity is verified.
**Do** identify device, source revision and capture/interaction limits when accepting UI work.
donts: **Don't** turn launcher artwork colors or screenshot samples into a screen palette.
**Don't** copy the retained Kotlin reference's raw-pixel insets or four-button row into shared phone standards.
**Don't** invent a custom typeface, radius, shadow scale or browser approximation of native rendering.
**Don't** treat disconnected screenshots, synthetic tests or builds as physical accessibility, Bluetooth, source-audio or whole-product acceptance.
**Don't** treat square icon catalogs or software-mask previews as actual iPhone, Android monochrome-theme or layered Icon Composer acceptance.
